This document provides an example of forecasting using Winter’s Method. The data used consists of RIT’s energy demand data.

Task 1

In this part, the flowchart for making decision on Exponential smoothing method is provided.

Figure 1: Exponential smoothing method decision flowchart

Based on this flowchart, the Holt Winter’s Method-Additive is good for the demand data of RIT because we have seasonal pattern in this data and also the amplitude of this pattern is independent from average level of season.

Reading the data and aggregating it

First of all, I read the data set and changed the format of date, then I hourly aggregated the data

Here I provide the graph of whole data set after imputing missing values

Figure 2: Graph of Original Data

Splitting data and Providing difficult and easy test week

I have considered the Christmas week of 2019 as a difficult week and I have used the data from 2019 as training set.

Figure 3: Graph of Difficult test set

Figure 4: Graph of Difficult tarin set

I have considered a normal week in the spring semester of 2019 as a easy week, then I have used the data from 2018 and 2019 to train model.

Figure 5: Graph of Easy test set

Figure 6: Graph of Easy tarin set

Defining test and train set for difficult and easy weeks

The training and test set for difficult and easy week are provided.

DifficultTrainSet <- imputedLVCF[DifficultTrainStart<=imputedLVCF$Time & imputedLVCF$Time<= DifficultTrainEnd,]
DifficultTestSet <- imputedLVCF[DifficultTestStart<=imputedLVCF$Time & imputedLVCF$Time<=DifficultTestEnd,]

EasyTrainSet <- imputedLVCF[EasyTrainstart<=imputedLVCF$Time & imputedLVCF$Time<= EasyTrainEnd,]
EasyTestSet <- imputedLVCF[EasyTestStart<=imputedLVCF$Time & imputedLVCF$Time<= EasyTestEnd,]

DifficultTrainingTS <- ts(DifficultTrainSet$net_demand,freq=168)
EasyTrainTS <- ts(EasyTrainSet$net_demand,freq=168)

Training Holt Winter’s Method

In this section, I have used Holt Winter additive method to tain the difficult data set and easy data set. I did not quantify parameters of this model and just allowed R programming language to use the best parameters. The plots for original training data and smoothed data are provided here.

hwDifficult<-HoltWinters(DifficultTrainingTS,seasonal="additive")
hwEasy<-HoltWinters(EasyTrainTS,seasonal="additive")

Figure 7: Exponentially smoothed data using Winters Method

Figure 8: Exponentially smoothed data using Winters Method

Figure 14: Fancy Residuals plot for Easy Week

Based on these four plots on the easy week, we could conclude that our selected model with its unique parameters acts well and it is shown that errors are normally distributed, they almost have an average of zero which is good. Their variability over time has not changed, so this is good. Overall, we could result that the selected model on the easy week has good performance.

For the difficult week, the plots are residuals also are provided. These plots show more variance and change in residuals over time and the normal probability of these residuals also has more differences according to the specified line. All of these differences between the difficult week data set and easy week data set is not that much, so overall our selected model acts good on both training data sets.
